checks: No eclipse at 2 of 53 covered epochs where the 2.43205 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 394942247 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.4321 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse that dims the system by 29.27%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal stands out strongly in automated analysis, with a box-least-squares detection significance of 908.9 and a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 303.9. The pixel-level centroid offset of 2.8 arcseconds from the target position was measured and analyzed. This candidate does not appear in any of six checked variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.78 suggests the automated pipeline considers it a plausible real target, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
